answer: I'd like to describe something I saw in the night sky a few years ago, which I still think about. Something genuinely interesting I once saw in the sky was a spectacular meteor shower during a stay at my grandparents' home in our ancestral village. The village is far from any city lights, which made the night sky incredibly clear. My cousin, who follows these things online, told me the shower was expected, so a group of us, including my younger sister, stayed up late and lay on a mat in the courtyard to watch. It was a cool, clear night in December, just after the rice harvest. When the first streaks of light shot across the sky, we were all completely [[mesmerised]]. It was a genuinely [[awe-inspiring]] sight, and the sheer scale of the universe suddenly felt very real. We lay there for over an hour, gasping each time a bright meteor appeared. Even my grandfather came out to join us for a while and told us about the stars he used to navigate by as a young man. What made it so special was the shared sense of wonder among us. Some of the younger cousins fell asleep on the mat, but I stayed awake until the very end. Honestly, in towns and cities we forget how [[magnificent]] the night sky can be. That experience left me feeling small in the best possible way, and it sparked a lasting fascination with astronomy. It is a memory I will always find genuinely [[humbling]], and it made me appreciate the [[unspoilt]] darkness of the countryside.

followUps.q: Do you often look at the stars?
followUps.answer: Not as often as I would like. In Sirajganj there is a bit too much light at night, but whenever we visit the village, I make a point of stepping outside after dinner to look up.

followUps.q: Would you like to learn more about astronomy?
followUps.answer: Yes, I would. I have started reading about it a little, and one day I would love to look through a proper telescope and see the rings of Saturn with my own eyes.

note: Set in the grandparents' village with cousin, sister and grandfather; added 'unspoilt'.
